title: bug: chat_pin and chat_unpin record no actor on PIN_CREATED / PIN_REMOVED (chat_unpin takes no workerId, StateManager.unpinMessage takes no actor, and pinnedBy lives only in PIN_CREATED's payload), so get_activity_log by workerId misses every pin change
description:
Filed by governor-e6b40560 from item 1 of defect hunt #8's held-back list (task-21d671c1, architect-1dd28c7c, #governors msg-adb6f774). The hunt held it until task-3e1d0c2e landed, because the fix touches StateManager.ts. 3e1d0c2e is DONE (f8b8d60c).

PROBLEM (verified by reading moe/work-2026-10-24 at f8b8d60c)
- get_activity_log { workerId } keeps only events whose own workerId matches (tools/getActivityLog.ts:131-132). That field is set from `worker?.id || proposal?.workerId || actorWorkerId` (state/activityLog.ts:83).
- state/chatStore.ts:542 appends `PIN_CREATED` with `{ channelId, messageId, pinnedBy }` and no actorWorkerId. The pinner shows up only in the payload, so the per-seat filter never matches.
- state/chatStore.ts:559 appends `PIN_REMOVED` with `{ channelId, messageId }` and no actor at all.
- tools/chatUnpin.ts declares no workerId property (:11-15). StateManager.unpinMessage(channelId, messageId) (StateManager.ts:927-928) has no actor parameter.
- The actor family (c05bf92d, 2e3012b9, d981e0b0, e977c32b, 1064df99, 3e1d0c2e) records the caller as the event's actor everywhere else.

EFFECT
A per-seat audit cannot see who pinned or unpinned a message. Pins are the governor's and humans' todo and reference list.

DEPENDENCY
dependsOn task-3064fd45 (PLANNING). That row gives chat_pin chat_send's sender guard ("system" refused NOT_ALLOWED, unregistered ids refused INVALID_INPUT) and resolves chat_pin's and chat_unpin's channel reference. Its DoD limits its diff to chatPin.ts, chatUnpin.ts and chatPin.test.ts. This row builds on that guard: the actor it records should be the validated caller, and chat_unpin's new workerId should get the same guard. Plan against 3064fd45's plan. WORKING claims wait until it is DONE.

FIX DIRECTION (the architect decides)
- Thread an optional actorWorkerId through chatStore pinMessage and unpinMessage and their StateManager wrappers into appendActivity, as 3e1d0c2e did for the epic tools.
- chat_pin passes its validated workerId.
- chat_unpin accepts the proxy-injected workerId, guards it like chat_pin and passes it on.
- The /ws PIN_MESSAGE and UNPIN_MESSAGE paths (WebSocketServer.ts ~1125-1143) keep working. Recording 'human' there, as /ws already passes for pinnedBy, is optional.
- Payloads stay the same, pinnedBy included.

Gate: narrow, per the epic-be924fb8 ruling msg-bbf4f109. Run the chat pin test files plus StateManager.test.ts and WebSocketServer.test.ts.
definitionOfDone: chat_pin and chat_unpin record the caller's workerId as the actor on PIN_CREATED and PIN_REMOVED, so get_activity_log { workerId } returns both events for that seat; the PIN_CREATED payload is unchanged (pinnedBy kept).

chat_unpin accepts the caller's workerId and applies the same sender guard chat_pin has after task-3064fd45 ("system" refused NOT_ALLOWED, an unregistered id refused INVALID_INPUT, "human" allowed); the /ws pin and unpin paths still work.

A daemon regression test fails before the fix and passes after it, and `npx vitest run src/state/StateManager.test.ts src/server/WebSocketServer.test.ts` plus the chat pin test files stay green (run in a snapshot outside the shared checkout).

implementationPlan.description:
Thread the actor through the pin store and its wrapper (chatStore.ts, StateManager.ts). This follows the f8b8d60c pattern: a trailing optional `actorWorkerId?: string` that ends up as appendActivity's 7th argument. That argument is the event's workerId (activityLog.ts:83), the field the get_activity_log filter reads (getActivityLog.ts:131-132).

(a) chatStore.ts pinMessage (:517-545). Make the PIN_CREATED append (:542) `state.appendActivity('PIN_CREATED', { channelId, messageId, pinnedBy }, undefined, undefined, undefined, undefined, pinnedBy)`.
- pinnedBy already IS the validated caller on both paths: chat_pin's guarded workerId (after task-3064fd45) and /ws PIN_MESSAGE's 'human' (WebSocketServer.ts:1127).
- So pinMessage's signature, chatPin.ts and WebSocketServer.ts all stay unchanged.

(b) chatStore.ts unpinMessage (:547-561).
- Add a trailing `actorWorkerId?: string` and pass it as the 7th argument of the PIN_REMOVED append (:559).
- Keep the payload exactly `{ channelId, messageId }`. The description says payloads stay as they are.

(c) StateManager.ts wrapper (:927-929): `async unpinMessage(channelId: string, messageId: string, actorWorkerId?: string): Promise<void> { return unpinMessage(this, channelId, messageId, actorWorkerId); }`. Touch no other method: task-3e1d0c2e's epic and task methods are DONE and are not yours.

Out of scope:
- The /ws UNPIN_MESSAGE call (WebSocketServer.ts:1141) passes no actor, so a board unpin keeps recording none, as today. The description calls 'human' there optional, and leaving it keeps the diff to 5 files.
- PIN_TOGGLED (togglePinDone, /ws only).

Error handling: the 'Channel not found', 'Message not found in channel', 'Message already pinned' and 'Pin not found' throws all stay before the append, unchanged. An omitted actor records exactly what HEAD records.
implementationPlan.note: pinMessage passes pinnedBy as appendActivity's 7th arg (actor); unpinMessage + StateManager.unpinMessage gain trailing optional actorWorkerId forwarded to PIN_REMOVED. Payloads unchanged.

implementationPlan.description:
chat_unpin accepts the caller's workerId, guards it and passes it on (chatUnpin.ts).

This row depends on task-3064fd45, so the file you start from already resolves the channel (resolveChannelRef, then notFound) and calls `state.unpinMessage(channel.id, params.messageId)`. Read that landed version first.

(a) Schema.
- Add `workerId: { type: 'string', description: 'Worker removing the pin (a registered worker or "human"; omitted means "human")' }` to inputSchema.properties.
- Do NOT add it to `required`. That keeps the change additive: "No breaking changes to MCP tool API contracts". The proxy stamps a workerId on every agent call anyway.

(b) Guard. Apply chat_send's sender rule (chatSend.ts:40-53), in the compact form task-3064fd45 gave chatPin.ts.
- `if (params.workerId !== undefined && typeof params.workerId !== 'string') throw invalidInput('workerId', 'must be a string')`
- `const actor = params.workerId || 'human'`
- `if (actor === 'system') throw notAllowed('chat_unpin as "system"', 'reserved for daemon-internal messages')`
- `if (actor !== 'human' && !state.getWorker(actor) && !state.tryLoadWorkerFromDisk(actor)) throw invalidInput('workerId', 'Unknown sender: workerId must be a registered worker or "human"')`
- Put the guard after the existing channel and messageId string checks and BEFORE the channel resolution and the store call. Refuse 'system' before the registry lookup, so it gets NOT_ALLOWED and not INVALID_INPUT.
- Import notAllowed.

(c) Call `state.unpinMessage(channel.id, params.messageId, actor)`.

Error handling: every refusal comes before the store call, so a refused unpin writes no pins file, emits no PINS_UPDATED and appends no PIN_REMOVED. The response shape stays `{ success: true }`.
implementationPlan.note: chat_unpin: optional workerId (not required), actor = workerId||'human', 'system' -> NOT_ALLOWED before registry lookup, unregistered -> INVALID_INPUT, all before channel resolution and store call; actor passed to state.unpinMessage.

implementationPlan.description:
Tests in chatPin.test.ts. task-3064fd45 created this file; it lands before this row (dependsOn), so extend it. It is listed as newFiles only because HEAD at planning time (f8b8d60c) does not have it yet.

Reuse its fixture and helpers: h, generalId(), send, pin, unpin, posted(), expectNoPin(). Import getActivityLogTool from './getActivityLog.js'. Before reading events, call `await flushActivityLog(h.state)`.

Add one describe block:
(a1) chat_pin as 'worker-a' records PIN_CREATED with event.workerId 'worker-a'. Its payload deep-equals `{ channelId: generalId(), messageId, pinnedBy: 'worker-a' }` (unchanged).
(a2) A pin as 'human', then an unpin as 'worker-a', records PIN_REMOVED with event.workerId 'worker-a'. Its payload deep-equals `{ channelId, messageId }`.
(a3) `getActivityLogTool(h.state).handler({ workerId: 'worker-a', eventTypes: ['PIN_CREATED', 'PIN_REMOVED'] }, h.state)` returns exactly those two events for the seat. Assert the event names and ids, not only a count.
(a4) chat_unpin with workerId 'system' rejects { code: MoeErrorCode.NOT_ALLOWED }; with 'worker-ghost' it rejects { code: MoeErrorCode.INVALID_INPUT }. Each time the pin is still listed in h.state.getPins(generalId()), and no PIN_REMOVED was appended.
(a5) chat_unpin as 'human', and chat_unpin with workerId omitted, each succeed and record PIN_REMOVED with workerId 'human'.
(a6) The board path: `await h.state.unpinMessage(generalId(), messageId)` with no actor still removes the pin, and its PIN_REMOVED has no workerId (unchanged).

(a1)-(a5) fail on HEAD plus task-3064fd45: no actor is recorded, and chat_unpin has no guard.
implementationPlan.note: Extended chatPin.test.ts (landed by 3064fd45) with a 'pin events record the caller as actor' describe: a1-a6. First gate run: a3/a5 failed only because get_activity_log reads newest-first; assertions made order-independent; re-verified in step 5.

- a new line `workerId?: string  // Optional: worker removing the pin, a registered worker or "human" (omitted: "human"); same refusals as chat_pin`.

Add one note under the two sections: PIN_CREATED and PIN_REMOVED record the caller as the activity event's workerId, so get_activity_log { workerId } finds them. Payloads are unchanged.
